proposal.title: Ilosefosk: a signing and verification tool for source packages
proposal.summary: Ilosefosk builds a signing and verification tool for source packages for maintainers of open source libraries.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Most source packages are still published without a signature that users can check. Maintainers of open source libraries depend on package signing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a signing and verification tool for source packages called Ilosefosk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Package signing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/ilosefosk/ilosefosk, which 221 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on package signing for 4 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/ilosefosk/ilosefosk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 69250.00 EUR for 91 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Most source packages are still published without a signature that users can check. Maintainers of open source libraries depend on package signing every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a signing and verification tool for source packages called Ilosefosk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Package signing is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/ilosefosk/ilosefosk, which 221 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on package signing for 4 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/ilosefosk/ilosefosk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 69250.00 EUR for 91 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.
